therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus on metformin
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 52 and Week 104

results.effect_size: LS mean HbA1c change: alogliptin 25 mg -0.76% (Week 52), -0.72% (Week 104); alogliptin 12.5 mg -0.81% (Week 52), -0.68% (Week 104); glipizide -0.73% (Week 52), -0.59% (Week 104)
biomarker_changes: HbA1c reduced from baseline in all arms at Week 52 and Week 104
Fasting plasma glucose reduced more in alogliptin arms vs glipizide arm over time; glipizide arm showed FPG increase above baseline by Week 52
Body weight decreased in alogliptin arms (~-0.68 to -0.90 kg at Week 104) and increased in glipizide arm (~+0.95 kg at Week 104)
subgroup_findings: At Week 104, more alogliptin-treated patients achieved HbA1c ≤7.0% (45.6% and 48.5%) vs glipizide (42.8%)
At Week 104, more alogliptin-treated patients achieved HbA1c ≤6.5% (23.5% and 24.1%) vs glipizide (19.0%)
FPG diverged over time: alogliptin arms maintained reductions while glipizide arm returned to near-baseline or above by Week 52-104
safety_signals: Glipizide arm had numerically more acute myocardial infarctions (5 vs 0 and 1) and myocardial infarctions (3 vs 0 and 1)
Alogliptin 25 mg arm had numerically more cardiac failure events (3 vs 2 and 1)
Overall serious cardiovascular events were low across all arms

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose output and improves insulin sensitivity, complementing alogliptin's incretin-mediated insulin secretion to produce additive glycemic control
modulation_entries.citation: Alogliptin tablets; Metformin tablets combined in metformin_alogliptin arms showing sustained HbA1c reductions over 104 weeks
